summary: Sustained elevated 5xx for customer during large embedding fanout due to sidecar fairness throttle regression and upstream runtime OOMs
description:
Issue summary:
Maple Health AI reported a sustained spike in 5xx responses (502/503) during an embedding upload that fanout to multiple shards. Errors started 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC and continued for ~90 minutes before mitigation.

Impact:
- Customer-facing embedding API returned 10-30% 5xx for tenant Maple Health (dedicated pool).
- Ingest jobs for large embedding batches were failing, blocking their nightly processing.
- Observed elevated latency and increased runtime restarts leading to degraded throughput.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1, Dedicated capacity pool "dedicated-mh-01" for Maple Health AI.
- Affected model: text-embedding-3-small pinned at v2026-02-28.

Steps to reproduce (replicated by support on repro cluster):
1) Upload 20k small documents via bulk-embed endpoint with parallelism similar to customer (50 concurrent chunks).
2) Observe API gateway accept-queue growth and backpressure to sidecar rate-limiter.
3) After ~2–3 minutes, one or more runtime pods report rapidly increasing memory (growth) then restart.
4) Client sees 502/503 responses and retry storms amplify the problem.

Key logs and traces:
- apigw traces: increased 5xx tagging with upstream_reset and timeout. Trace IDs attached in investigation_notes.
- runtime logs: repeated allocation spikes followed by OOMKilled in kernels allocating kv-cache.
- sidecar logs: "fairness_window_exceeded" metrics spike and many transient 429->502 handoffs.
- Prometheus: rate_limiter_fairness_latency_bucket_sum jumped 18x at incident start.

Immediate customer communication:
- Support notified customer 2026-03-10 09:25 UTC and provided workaround (throttle client parallelism to <=8).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:27 — Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after initial customer report. Collected logs, requested heap dumps from runtime. Customer confirmed high parallelism during bulk upload.

2026-03-10 09:40 — Liam O'Connor (SRE): Observed sidecar throttle spikes on dedicated pool 'dedicated-mh-01'. Suggest rate-limiter policy rollback to previous stable hash-window. Spinning repro in staging to confirm.

2026-03-10 10:05 — Maple Health AI (Customer - tech@maplehealth.ai): Provided request IDs and confirmed they will pause their bulk job if we need to take immediate mitigations. Asked for ETA on fix, noting blocked nightly job.

2026-03-10 10:18 — SRE (Liam O'Connor): Rolled back sidecar rate-limiter config from rollout #187 to stable config (hash-window=256 -> 64) in dedicated-mh-01. Observed drop in fairness_window_exceeded metric and immediate reduction in 5xx.

2026-03-10 11:00 — Runtime eng (Nadia Singh): Investigated OOMs — found that when sidecar returned 429 frequently, runtime queued requests and kv-cache warmed inefficiently leading to memory pressure. Patch PR created to add backpressure-aware queue limit in serving runtime.

2026-03-11 08:12 — Customer (Maple Health AI): Confirmed nightly backfill completed after support guidance; requested long-term mitigation and assurance it won't recur. Asked for postmortem and timeline for runtime patch.

2026-03-12 14:30 — Liam O'Connor: Deployed serving-runtime backpressure fix (PR #1024) to canary, verified in staging with large embed simulation. No OOMs observed; scheduled gradual rollout to dedicated pool this evening. Marking ticket resolved after monitoring window.
2026-03-12 18:05 — Aisha Patel: Sent post-incident summary and recommended client-side parallelism limits. Customer acknowledged and closed with thanks.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:33 — Collected heap profiles from runtime pods (pod ids: runtime-mh-01-7f9, runtime-mh-01-8k2). Heap showed growth in 'kv_cache' region correlated to requests queued behind repeated 429s.
Sidecar rate-limiter change in rollout #187 introduced a fairness_window extension that made per-tenant tokens accumulate slower and caused head-of-line blocking for large fanouts on dedicated pools.
When sidecar returned 429 frequently, API gateway retried and runtime accepted transient bursts which increased memory retention for KV caches; combination led to OOMs and restarts.

Prometheus alert 'tenant_pipeline_error_rate' fired at 09:14 UTC. Grafana dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/secure/tenant-errors?orgId=1&var-tenant=maple-health. Slack incident channel: #support-maplehealth-482158.
resolution:
Mitigations applied:
- Immediate rollback of sidecar rate-limiter policy to previous stable config in dedicated-mh-01 (2026-03-10 10:20 UTC).
- Temporary increase of apigw per-tenant accept-queue soft-limit to reduce head-of-line retry amplification.
- Customer instructed to throttle client-side parallelism to <=8 concurrent chunk uploads during backfill windows.

Fixes delivered:\n- Serving-runtime PR #1024: introduces queue-length cap and backpressure-aware kv-cache admission to prevent memory growth while upstream returns 429s. Deployed to canary 2026-03-12 14:30 UTC, then rolled to dedicated pool 2026-03-12 17:45 UTC.\n- Sidecar change reverted in config repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar-rate-limiter/commit/9f4c2e8. New rollout will include a staged canary with 'fairness_window' telemetry gating.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Create a runbook entry for "sidecar fairness regression" with clear rollback steps (owner: SRE - Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-03-18.
- Add a synthetic test to CI that simulates large embedding fanout to validate fairness_window changes (owner: Runtime QE - Nadia Singh) — due 2026-03-22.
- Customer success check-in with Maple Health AI to validate no residual data loss and update SLA exceptions (owner: CS - Miguel Alvarez) — scheduled 2026-03-15.
